projects.title: AI Film Study
projects.summary: Two generated characters awaken inside an AI workspace. Believing themselves to be actors, they navigate cultural difference, shifting roles and the uncertain intentions of a creator.
projects.approach: A short AI film developed alongside a critical research report. The project asks how authorial control, character agency and cross-cultural representation become visible through the process of making an AI image.

projects.title: The dawn in Seoul
projects.summary: A fiction short exploring the difficulties faced by international students, and the distance between what can be felt and what can be expressed.
projects.approach: Written and directed during my master's studies in Korea. The project brings questions of language, belonging and cultural encounter into a lived, everyday setting.

projects.title: Dream Master
projects.summary: A dream becomes an explorable story. Players inhabit the perspective of an object, question furniture characters and gradually uncover the memories held by a room.
projects.approach: The project connects personal dream input, structured story creation, character dialogue and visual keepsakes. I am interested in the tension between a stable narrative structure and the possibilities of generative interaction. The prototype and planned platform remain distinct stages of the project.

projects.title: The trapped beast
projects.summary: A feature screenplay selected by Asian Art Film Festival 2026.
projects.approach: Part of my ongoing screenwriting practice, with attention to character perspective, fictional worlds and the relationship between individual choices and the narratives that contain them.
projects.selection: Screenplay selection ·  Asian Art Film Festival · 2026

projects.title: Kuang
projects.summary: A student psychology group crosses an ethical boundary by confining a fellow student in a dark, isolated room. As the participant’s mental state deteriorates, tensions within the group intensify. Interweaving the confinement footage with the group’s growing conflicts, the film traces how an experiment in control begins to unravel everyone involved.
projects.approach: Inspired by the enclosing structures in Francis Bacon’s paintings, The Frame explores confinement as both a physical condition and a psychological experience. The frame becomes a metaphor for rules, beliefs and obsessions that restrict individual freedom. Through its documentary-style presentation and parallel narratives, the film examines the relationship between power, observation and responsibility, suggesting that those who confine others also become trapped within the structures they create.

projects.title: Women Construction Workers
projects.summary: A documentary about women working on a construction site at Zhejiang University.
projects.approach: An early documentary practice grounded in observing work and everyday life, attending to people whose presence can be overlooked in familiar spaces.

projects.title: Glimmer
projects.summary: Films documenting a volunteer teaching programme in Yizhou, Guangxi.
projects.approach: A series of documentary and short-film works made around a volunteer teaching project, following the everyday exchanges that form a temporary community.

projects.title: Silence
projects.summary: n a dark commercial aquarium, Jiayi, a 25-year-old deaf keeper, forms a silent bond with Huanhuan, its star beluga. Separated by glass yet united by confinement, they mirror each other’s isolation. As increasingly demanding performances push both toward collapse, Huanhuan drags Jiayi into the depths—an ambiguous descent suspended between fatal violence, psychological escape, and a dream of freedom.
projects.approach: The film uses AI-generated imagery to construct its aquarium environments, underwater sequences, and encounters between human and animal. Kling’s motion control is used to develop Jiayi’s signing and subtle bodily gestures. Reflections, restricted spaces, and subdued lighting establish a claustrophobic visual language, while the imagined open sea offers a contrasting space of release. The process explores AI’s expressive possibilities through gesture, physical interaction, and shifts between psychological realism and dream imagery.

projects.title: The Bell of the Heart
projects.summary: Two people quietly fall for each other, yet neither finds the courage to express their feelings. As their affection remains unspoken, the possibility of a relationship gradually slips away, leaving them as strangers carrying the memory of what might have been.
projects.approach: The Bell of the Heart explores the distance between feeling and expression. Its emotional conflict emerges from mutual affection that never becomes a shared understanding. The story reflects on the vulnerability of making oneself known to another person, and on how hesitation can shape a relationship as profoundly as any spoken declaration. At its centre is the quiet loss of a connection that was possible but never realised.

projects.title: Mercury
projects.summary: A young woman’s relationship with two men unfolds across fragmented timelines, where affection, memory and coincidence become increasingly entangled. Through montage and a final narrative reversal, the music video raises an unresolved question: does she love the person before her, or the shadow of someone else she sees in him?
projects.approach: Mercury explores how memory and emotional projection shape romantic attachment. Montage connects displaced moments in time, while alternating warm and cool colour palettes express shifts in the characters’ emotional states. Building a complete dramatic narrative around the song, the work uses coincidence and reversal to examine a familiar uncertainty: whether love recognises another person as they are, or transforms them into an image of someone we cannot let go.

projects.title: INS — Concept Commercial
projects.summary: An AI-assisted concept commercial exploring cinematic atmosphere, visual rhythm and experimental storytelling.

profile.bio: I'm Yaojia Zeng, a screenwriter and filmmaker working across fiction, AI-assisted moving images and interactive narrative. I studied Broadcasting and Television at Zhejiang University and am pursuing a master's in Film and Moving Image Media at Chung-Ang University's Graduate School of Arts in Korea.
profile.style: My practice moves between everyday experience and imagined worlds. I return to nested stories, unstable perspectives and moments when a character starts to question the story they inhabit. Cultural encounters, the limits of language and the imagined inner lives of objects give these questions a form. I use AI as a material to examine through creative practice, while keeping the choices of the writer and filmmaker visible.
profile.interests:
AI-assisted moving-image practice and authorship
Metafiction, screenwriting and narrative structure
East Asian screen cultures and cross-cultural storytelling
Interactive narrative, object perspectives and character agency
